methods: writing x^x as e^(x ln x)
statement: Using the fact that $x^{x}=e^{x\\ln x}$, find $\\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{x})$.
solution: Let $y=x^{x}=e^{x\\ln x}$. Then $\\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{x\\ln x}\\cdot\\frac{d}{dx}(x\\ln x)=x^{x}\left(\\ln x+1\\right)$. Hence $\\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{x})=x^{x}(1+\\ln x)$ for $x>0$.
